title: Azure providers rewrite the caller's last message in place (assistant -> ai), corrupting content and crashing on multimodal input
author: Hexecu

comments.author: Hexecu
comments.body: Already have a fix up for this in #5731 — applies the rewrite to a deepcopy that only goes to the model, keeps the caller's messages intact, and guards for non-string content so multimodal input doesn't crash. Covers both Azure providers. Verified against a live Azure deployment.

comments.author: kartik-mem0
comments.body:
## Triage Notes

**What we've established:**
- Both `AzureOpenAILLM` and `AzureOpenAIStructuredLLM` apply `messages[-1]["content"] = user_prompt.replace("assistant", "ai")` in place — which mutates the caller's list, corrupts any occurrence of the substring (not just the role literal), and crashes on multimodal content where `content` is a list rather than a string.
- The original intent (avoiding Azure's "Indirect Attacks" content filter, tracked in #2636/#2937) is sound, but the implementation touches the caller's own data structure.
- Scope is narrow: Azure-only, triggered only when the last user message contains the substring "assistant" or when multimodal content is passed.

**Reproduction:** Confirmed (code tracing; multimodal crash reproducible without Azure credentials)
**Root cause:** `mem0/llms/azure_openai.py` and `mem0/llms/azure_openai_structured.py` rewrite `messages[-1]["content"]` on the original list rather than working on a copy, and do not guard for `content` being a list type.

**Next step:** PR #5731 fixes this by applying the rewrite to a deep copy — review feedback will be posted there.
